h1: The 7 Best HEPA Upright Vacuums for Allergies and Pet Hair, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best HEPA Upright Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 HEPA upright vacuums compared on filtration design, bagged vs bagless, pet tools, weight and budget.
summary: The Shark NV752 Rotator TruePet is the best HEPA upright for most homes, pairing a sealed filtration approach with a lift-away design and a pet-focused brush. The Kenmore Elite 31150 is the pick for allergy households that prefer a bagged machine with triple HEPA, and the Bissell CleanView Max Allergen is a strong value for pet owners. The Shark Navigator NV356E is the cheaper, lighter step into HEPA.
intro: The word HEPA on a vacuum box is the easiest claim in the category to make and the hardest to verify. A true HEPA filter only helps if the machine is sealed, so that dirty air cannot slip around it through gaps in the housing, and plenty of uprights with a HEPA filter leak at the seams. Buyers who care about allergies should read the design, not just the label.

We reviewed seven HEPA uprights from their listings, specification details and documentation, and ranked them on how seriously they approach filtration, how practical they are for pet hair, and how easy they are to empty and maintain. The listings for several models are short on numbers, so where a feature is not stated, we say so rather than fill in the gaps.

products.name: Shark NV752 Rotator Powered Lift-Away TruePet Upright Vacuum with HEPA Filter
products.verdict: A lift-away upright with a large dust cup, LED headlights and the most reliable sealed HEPA approach here.
products.description:
Shark pitches the NV752 at pet owners: the Rotator head comes with the Perfect Pet Power Brush, a generous dust cup, headlights built into the nozzle, and upholstery and crevice attachments, all behind a HEPA filter. The Lift-Away name describes the detachable pod that lets you carry the canister for stairs and above-floor jobs.

It ranks first because it combines the broadest set of tools with the most credible filtration story in the group. LED headlights are more useful than they sound, since they show hair and crumbs along baseboards that a normal light misses. The cost is price: it sits in the $200 to $500 bucket, higher than most others here, and the Rotator is heavier than the budget Navigators.

Buy it if you have pets, a mix of carpet and hard floors, and want a single vacuum that handles stairs and furniture too. Skip it if weight is your main concern, because the lift-away design adds bulk.

products.name: Kenmore Elite 31150 Pet Friendly Bagged Upright Beltless Vacuum, Triple HEPA
products.verdict: Bagged, beltless and fitted with triple HEPA, a 3D inducer motor and a telescoping wand.
products.description:
Kenmore's Elite 31150 takes the bagged route and drops the drive belt entirely. Filtration is Triple HEPA, the motor is a 3D Inducer, and you get a telescoping wand, five height positions and the Pet Handi-Mate among three included tools.

Bagged construction is the quiet advantage for allergy sufferers. Dirt goes into a sealed bag that you lift out without a cloud of dust, which a bagless cup cannot always promise. Beltless also means there is no drive belt to snap, so one common repair job disappears. It ranks below the Shark because the Shark is the more modern all-round package, and because bags are a running cost.

Buy it if dust exposure at emptying time matters to you. Skip it if you dislike buying bags or want a lift-away pod.
cons: Replacement bags are a recurring cost
products.idealFor: Allergy households that prefer bagged vacuums.

products.name: Bissell CleanView Max Allergen Upright Vacuum with HEPA Filtration, 4377
products.verdict: A tangle-free brush roll and a TurboEraser pet tool at a $100 to $200 price.
products.description:
Bissell's CleanView Max Allergen brings a tangle-free brush roll and a TurboEraser pet tool together with HEPA filtration, for $100 to $200. The tangle-free roll is the feature that matters for long-haired pets and owners, because wrapped hair is the most common reason a vacuum loses suction.

It ranks third because it delivers the pet-hair basics at a much lower price than the Shark. What it gives up is the lift-away flexibility and the sealed-system credibility that the NV752 documents. Against the Navigator below, it is the more pet-focused of the two, with the extra tool.

It is the right buy for a pet household on a moderate budget. Skip it if you need the strongest allergen story, because the listing offers fewer filtration details.
pros: Tangle-free brush roll fights wrapped hair
HEPA filtration at a moderate price
products.idealFor: Pet owners with a mid-range budget.

products.name: Shark Navigator Lift-Away Vacuum, HEPA, Pet Hair, White/Silver, NV356E
products.verdict: The affordable Navigator with HEPA and a lift-away pod for pets and allergies.
products.description:
Aimed at households juggling pets and allergies, the NV356E is a Navigator Lift-Away that adds HEPA filtration for $100 to $200, and the Lift-Away design gives you a portable canister for stairs, upholstery and ceiling corners.

It ranks fourth because it offers the Shark approach at a lower price than the NV752, though without the powered brush roll and the extra tools of the premium model. It also trails the Bissell in pet-specific tools, since the listing mentions pet hair but does not detail a dedicated pet brush. The compromise is a plainer feature set for a lower outlay.

Buy it if you want Shark's lift-away layout at a middle price. Skip it if you have heavy pet shedding and want a specialised pet tool.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a lift-away Shark for less.

products.name: Oreck HEPA Upright Vacuum Cleaner, Lightweight Bagged Upright Vac
products.verdict: A lightweight bagged HEPA upright aimed at allergy-sensitive households.
products.description:
The Oreck is a lightweight bagged upright with HEPA filtration, aimed at allergy-sensitive households. The listing offers few numbers, so what you are buying is the concept: a bagged machine that is easy to lift, with the sealed-bag emptying advantage.

It ranks fifth because the listing does not detail a pet tool, a brush roll type or a bag capacity, which makes it harder to recommend over the Kenmore Elite that spells out its features. The light weight is a real benefit for older users, upstairs rooms and anyone who moves the vacuum often.

It suits a small home with hard floors and thin carpet. Skip it if you have a lot of pet hair or thick pile, where a bigger machine with a dedicated pet brush would serve you better.
products.idealFor: Small homes and users who want a light vacuum.
products.skipIf: You have heavy pet shedding or thick carpet.

products.name: Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off, HEPA, 39883
products.verdict: A pet-hair upright with HEPA and a lift-off design, positioned for lower weight.
products.description:
The Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off combines the name of Bissell's pet range with HEPA filtration and a lift-off design, and it sits in the $100 to $200 bucket. The Lift-Off wording indicates a detachable portion for portable cleaning.

It ranks sixth because the listing is thin on details, so it is hard to rate its brush roll or its tools against the CleanView Max Allergen above. Weight is its main sales angle, which suits people who struggle with a heavy upright on stairs.

Buy it if you want pet hair help in a lighter body. Skip it if you want the documentation and tool set of a more fully described model.
pros: Pet hair focus in a lighter build
products.idealFor: Pet owners who want less weight to push.
products.skipIf: You want full tool and filter documentation.

products.name: Kenmore Featherlite Lift-Up Bagless Upright Vacuum
products.verdict: A budget bagless Kenmore for buyers who want HEPA filtration at a lower price.
products.description:
The Featherlite Lift-Up is a bagless Kenmore upright in the $100 to $200 bucket, positioned for buyers who want HEPA filtration for less. The listing gives very few specifications.

It ranks last because there is little to confirm how it handles pet hair, what tools come with it, or how sealed the filtration is. Bagless also means emptying a cup, which releases dust more easily than a bagged machine, and that matters for allergy sufferers.

It is a fair buy for a household that wants a basic HEPA vacuum on a budget. Skip it if allergies drive the purchase and you want a bagged machine such as the Kenmore Elite.
pros: Bagless means no bags to buy
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want basic HEPA.

whatMatters.factor: A sealed system, not just a filter
whatMatters.detail: A HEPA filter only works if air has to pass through it. If the housing leaks, dirty air escapes around the filter and the label means little. Look for a stated sealed system or a bagged design, and treat a bare HEPA sticker as a starting point.

Bagged vacuums trap dust in a sealed bag that you lift out, which suits people with allergies. Bagless models save on bags but release dust when you empty the cup. Check which type a listing describes before you assume convenience.

whatMatters.factor: Pet hair tools and brush roll
whatMatters.detail: Pet hair wraps around a standard brush roll and chokes suction. A tangle-free roll, as on the Bissell CleanView Max Allergen, or a pet power brush, as on the Shark NV752, addresses that. Look for these names on the listing, not just the word pet.

Uprights are heavy, and stairs make that obvious. A lift-away or lift-off pod lets you carry just the canister to clean above the floor. Compare weight class and portability claims if you have multiple floors.

Bagged machines need replacement bags, and every HEPA filter eventually needs washing or replacing. The price bucket tells you the upfront cost only. Factor in the maintenance schedule before deciding.

faq.q: Does HEPA on the box mean the vacuum is allergy-safe?
faq.a: Not by itself. A HEPA filter needs a sealed housing so that air cannot bypass it, and the label does not guarantee that. Bagged designs like the Kenmore Elite 31150 help by containing dust until disposal.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with pet hair vacuums?
faq.a: They buy on suction alone. Hair wraps around a brush roll and cuts performance, so a tangle-free roll or pet power brush matters more than raw power. The Bissell CleanView Max and Shark NV752 both address this.

faq.q: Is the Shark NV752 worth it over the Navigator NV356E?
faq.a: If you have pets and want tools like the Perfect Pet Power Brush and LED headlights, yes. If you mainly want HEPA and a lift-away pod, the NV356E does the job in the $100 to $200 bucket.

faq.q: How do I set up a new upright?
faq.a: Most arrive with the handle and hose to attach, then you set the height and plug in. The Kenmore Elite has five height positions, so match the setting to your carpet pile before the first use.

faq.q: How do I maintain a HEPA filter?
faq.a: Check the manual for whether the filter is washable or replaceable, and clean or swap it on schedule. A clogged filter cuts suction and, in a HEPA system, can reduce the filtration benefit.

faq.q: Can I use these on hard floors?
faq.a: Yes, but check whether you can turn the brush roll off or adjust the height. A spinning roll can scatter debris on bare floors, so models with adjustable height such as the Kenmore Elite suit mixed flooring.

finalTake: The Shark NV752 Rotator TruePet is the best HEPA upright here for homes with pets, stairs and mixed floors. The Kenmore Elite 31150 is the better answer for allergy sufferers who prefer bags, and the Bissell CleanView Max Allergen gives pet owners the most for a moderate budget. The Shark Navigator NV356E is the sensible step down if you want lift-away flexibility for less. Judge any HEPA claim by how the machine seals.
